transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-04
Time: 14:00 PT
Duration: 55 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood SE), Evan Liu (Meridian CTO), Marisol Torres (ML Engineer), Samir Patel (Infra), Aisha Rahman (Product)

Auto-summary: (auto) Discussed latency/throughput targets, sample prompt benchmarking, deployment modes and security requirements.

[00:00:00] Jordan (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I think we got most folks. Uh hi Evan, thanks for taking the time. Quick intents, we're here to understand your latency and throughput goals and figure out whether Hosted, Dedicated or Private fits best.

[00:00:22] Evan (Meridian): Yep thanks Jordan. We want to be concise - our main KPIs are p95 latency for chat responses and sustained token/sec throughput. For short queries, p95 ideally <200ms, for longer streaming replies maybe up to 500ms is acceptable. We also care about concurrency: up to 5k concurrent users during peak.

[00:00:45] Priya (Redwood SE): Great, and when you say streaming, are you doing server-side streaming token-by-token to clients, or do clients poll?

[00:00:52] Marisol (Meridian): It's token streaming to clients. The UI renders tokens as they arrive. Latency to first-token is critical.

[00:01:05] Liam (Redwood): Got it. For streaming-first-token p95 targets, we usually look at the model variant, quantization, and whether KV cache hits are present. Also whether you need context-window long histories - that affects kernel selection.

[00:01:28] Samir (Meridian Infra): Also want to call out security: we'll likely need private networking (VPC), KMS-managed keys, and SOC2 evidence. How does Redwood handle on-prem / private deployments vs hosted?

[00:01:42] Jordan (Redwood): Short answer: Hosted is fastest to get started, Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools and SLAs, and Private gives a customer-controlled control plane for VPC/on-prem. All support KMS/HSM integration; we can share our security one-pager.

[00:02:05] Evan: Cool. In terms of raw numbers: we did an internal benchmark that shows our current infra can do ~150 tokens/sec per GPU at 16-bit; but when we hit concurrency of ~2k clients latency spikes. We need Redwood to demonstrate scaling to 5k concurrent streaming sessions with p95 under 500ms and ideally under 200ms for short queries.

[00:02:28] Priya: That helps. For benchmarking we'll need sample prompts and typical context length distribution - do you have that?

[00:02:33] Marisol: Yes, we'll share a set of 75 prompts: short, medium, long. Average turn length is ~40 tokens for short, 120 for medium, 400 for long.

[00:02:47] Jordan: Perfect. We'll run token/sec benchmarks with those. Quick clarifying Q: What's your tolerance for cold start vs warm-cache? Are you okay assuming warmed KV cache for p95?

[00:02:56] Evan: Production should be warmed, but we understand a cold-start tail - main KPI is steady state p95.

[00:03:10] Liam: OK. For Hosted vs Dedicated math: Hosted can handle bursts but has multi-tenant variability; Dedicated gives predictable throughput and latency with reserved GPU pools. Private mirrors Dedicated but adds customer networking and on-prem control - there's more ops overhead.

[00:03:29] Samir: For Private, what's the approach to autoscaling and burst capacity? If we have a sudden 2x traffic spike, can we rely on autoscaling without breaking p95?

[00:03:38] Priya: Yes, Dedicated supports autoscaling policies and burst capacity; you can configure cushion pools. We'll show historical scaling behavior from other customers. For Private, autoscaling depends on your infra; Redwood's control plane can still orchestrate but you manage the physical capacity or cloud nodes.

[00:03:59] Evan: And in terms of cost/capacity tradeoffs, what's the unit economics like? i.e., cost per 1k concurrent streaming sessions?

[00:04:08] Jordan: We'll share a model in the pricing sheet - rough thumb: batching and KV cache reduces per-token cost significantly. Also quantization choice matters: int8 vs int4 moves cost down but can affect quality.

[00:04:20] Marisol: About quantization, we need to preserve answer quality. We can't drop quality for cost savings in a way that breaks product metrics. We do evals.

[00:04:28] Priya: Totally. Redwood Optimize gives recommendations for quantization + batching per workload. For your prompt set we can run regressed evals to show quality delta.

[00:04:40] Evan: Great. For the benchmark, what metrics will you provide? p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, GPU utilization, and a breakdown by model variant?

[00:04:50] Priya: Yes - we'll return p50/p90/p95/p99, tokens/sec sustained, tail latency graphs, concurrency profile, and per-token cost estimate. We'll also include traces for time-to-first-token and time-per-token for streaming.

[00:05:07] Liam: One caveat: transcription sometimes mixes up product names - sorry, little humor - but we will include detailed notes.

[00:05:14] Samir: About networking: if we go Private, we need SAML SSO, RBAC, audit logs shipped to our SIEM, and support for customer-managed KMS keys. Are those supported?

[00:05:23] Jordan: Yes - SSO via SAML, RBAC, audit logs, and KMS integrations are supported. We'll attach our SOC2 / security docs. There may be slight differences in operational model for on-prem versus VPC.

[00:05:40] Evan: Excellent. Another question: Model fallbacks and graceful degradation - if a high-quality model is unavailable, can Redwood route to a cheaper/quantized variant automatically?

[00:05:49] Priya: Yes, smart routing can fallback to compatible model variants by policy (latency, cost, region). We can configure automatic fallback with thresholds.

[00:06:02] Marisol: For latency numbers, what's the typical p95 for a 2k sequence with a modern 70B quantized model on Dedicated GPUs? Ballpark?

[00:06:12] Liam: Ballpark's tough without specifics, but for token/sec: with int8 on A100-class equivalent, we often see X tokens/sec - (transcription note: speaker said X, they meant ~120-200 tokens/sec depending on seq len). For p95, short prompts can be <200ms; long sequences will be higher. We'll produce concrete numbers in the benchmark.

[00:06:36] Evan: Understood. Can you do a focused bench on time-to-first-token (TTFT) since that's user-facing?

[00:06:41] Priya: Absolutely. We'll measure TTFT for 95th and 99th percentiles, with and without KV cache hits, and for streaming.

[00:06:54] Samir: One operational question: we have a compliance window - all logs older than 90 days must be purged and some data can't leave the VPC. Can Redwood support configurable retention and in-VPC-only logs for Private?

[00:07:05] Jordan: Yes, Private supports customer-managed data retention and in-VPC controls. Hosted has retention options but for stricter needs Private is the right fit.

[00:07:15] Evan: Good. Let's talk timeline: ideally we'd run a POC in two weeks, benchmarks in week one, and then evaluate Dedicated contract in 4-6 weeks. Does that sound feasible?

[00:07:27] Jordan: That timeline sounds reasonable. We'll need your prompts and some authorization for Redwood to run load tests against sample endpoints.

[00:07:36] Marisol: We'll provide prompts and a traffic shape. For authorization, Samir will work with Jordan on IP allow-lists for the test.

[00:07:44] Samir: Correct. I'll coordinate allow-listing and confirm KMS key access for test instrumentation.

[00:07:52] Priya: On the bench specifics, we'll run multiple scenarios: 1) Warmed KV cache, 2) Cold start, 3) Sustained streaming at 1k, 3k, 5k concurrency, and 4) Quantized variants (int8/int4) to show cost/quality tradeoffs.

[00:08:15] Evan: That covers what I want to see. Also please include model rollbacks and automatic fallback behavior in the runbook.

[00:08:22] Jordan: Will do. Any other questions on data residency, SSO, or legal?

[00:08:29] Aisha (Product): One small ask: can you show per-route cost breakdown (e.g., chat vs embeddings) in the report?

[00:08:36] Priya: Yes, we'll include token-level cost breakdown and per-route analytics.

[00:08:42] Evan: Great. If results look good, we'll move to a Dedicated reserved capacity conversation and then evaluate Private for compliance-sensitive workloads.

[00:08:52] Jordan: Makes sense. I'll recap next steps and attach docs.

[00:09:00] Jordan: Recap: 1) Meridian to share 75 sample prompts and traffic shape (Evan/Marisol) by 2026-06-06. 2) Redwood (Priya) to run benchmark scenarios and share logs and summary by 2026-06-09. 3) Jordan to send pricing + security docs by 2026-06-07. 4) Schedule Private networking deep dive for 2026-06-10 (Samir + Redwood SE).

[00:09:25] Evan: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.

[00:09:28] (crosstalk)

[00:09:35] Jordan: Thanks all. We'll follow up via email with invite and artifacts.

[00:09:40] (meeting ends)

Notes: Transcription occasionally swapped 'KV cache' with 'KV cash', 'TTFT' spelled out or mis-heard, and product names sometimes abbreviated. References shared: Redwood performance deck (link to drive), Hosted vs Dedicated pricing spreadsheet (link), security one-pager (link).
